component.name: U-Stu Video Editor
component.summary: Non-linear video editor built on GTK4, libadwaita and MLT

description.p: U-Stu is a multi-track video editor for GNOME, made for livestream and promo editing at 1080p and 4K. This is a beta for testers: expect rough edges, and please attach the log files to any report.

ul.li: Import footage, pictures and whole folders, then cut, trim, move and close gaps on any number of video and audio tracks
Play back with sound, with waveforms and thumbnails made in the background
Move, scale, rotate and crop pictures right on the preview
Proxies for smooth editing of large footage; exports always use the originals
Export to H.264 MP4

description.p: New since 0.78.4-beta.1:

ul.li: Moving pictures: a clip's position, size and rotation can change over time. The Transform card at the top of the Effects page pins, steps, eases and records them, with curves; dragging a keyframed picture on the preview sets a keyframe at the playhead.

Transitions: Additive, Screen and Lighten blend dissolves, Zoom In and Spin In, and the style tiles show your own two clips half-way through. A transition's sound can crossfade evenly (equal power) or cut at its middle.
A LUT or other file inside the project's folder is saved relative to it, so the project keeps it when the folder moves (such a project needs this version or newer).
Screen readers can reach the number fields in Settings, Render profiles, Edit Transform and U Stu Titles. U Stu Titles also has fixes for animated layers.
Dragging a picture in the preview is smoother, and dissolving from a still works.
Safety: the editor loads only the media modules it needs.

description.p: Try keyframing a picture's position with the Transform card, a Zoom In or a blend dissolve between two clips, and moving a project folder that uses a LUT. Install the Titles and Effects add-ons of this same version with the app.
New since 0.78.0-beta.1 (fixes):

ul.li: With GPU acceleration on, a flipped clip shows mirrored in place; a cropped or rotated flipped clip no longer comes out turned, smeared or out of its box.
Effects: the Add page no longer holds on to a clip's memory (about 180 MB for a 1080p clip), and two crashes are fixed, one on the Add page and one at quit.
U Stu Titles no longer crashes when you close it with a layer selected, and exporting or baking a title no longer crashes as it finishes.
A dissolve into a still or a colour clip works from its first frame.

description.p: Try long GPU playback with effects installed and watch the editor's memory, and flip a cropped or rotated clip with GPU acceleration on. Install the Titles and Effects add-ons of this same version with the app.

New since 0.78.2-beta.1: fixes for the Effects add-on. The Add page no longer renders its tiles while it's hidden, and its previews let go of your clip a moment after they're drawn: about 180 MB less for a 1080p clip. Two crashes with the add-on are fixed (a title selected before its template was picked, and quitting), and effects that need a graphics card's Vulkan, OpenCL, CUDA or VAAPI are no longer offered.
Try playing a long project with the Effects add-on installed and GPU acceleration on, with the Add page open for a while first, and watch the editor's memory stay level.

New since 0.78.0-beta.1: fixes in titles. U Stu Titles could crash when you closed it with a layer selected; it closes cleanly now. Exporting a title on its own, or baking a title clip, could crash as the export finished; it now waits for the encoder to finish first. And a caption clip's name on the timeline now follows its words when you edit them on the Title page, unless you renamed the clip.
Try selecting a layer in U Stu Titles, saving and closing it; and exporting a title a few times in a row, in different formats.

New since 0.77.0-beta.1: two title templates with an animated bell. In New Title's gallery, Lower third with ringing bell and Subscribe with ringing bell (under Bugs and badges) have a bell that rings every few seconds with a notification dot, in the Unicorn Tears colours.
Try one on a stream recording, change its text on the Title page, and export: the bell rings in the export as in the preview.

New since 0.73.1-beta.1, the last download: effects, transitions and animated titles. With the Effects add-on, press E for a tile of every effect on your clip; point to try one, click to add it. Keyframe values by pinning them, see and drag their curves under the clip (C), or record them as you play. Save sets of effects as looks, limit an effect to a rectangle or ellipse of the picture, pick colours from the picture, grade with .cube LUTs, and add adjustment blocks in the FX lane above the tracks to change everything beneath them for a stretch of time, fading in and out. Dissolves can dip, flash, slide, push or wipe (20 shapes): press T at a cut. Titles can carry Lottie animations. Importing thousands of clips is fast, playback restarts faster after an edit, and OpenFX plugins installed on the computer are no longer loaded unless you choose them.

Try an adjustment block over two clips with a fade at each end, a touch-recorded slider during playback, a LUT from your camera, and a wipe between two clips, then render and compare with the preview. Known limits: no zoom, spin or blend transitions yet; a clip's own position and size can't be keyframed yet; a project moved to another folder loses its LUTs. With GPU acceleration on, wipes can stutter at Full preview quality. The Effects and Titles add-ons come separately in the Flatpak.

New since 0.75.0-beta.1: animated layers in titles. In U Stu Titles, open + and choose Animation… to add a Lottie animation (the .json files LottieFiles and After Effects export). It plays in the designer, on the editor's timeline and in exports, once or over and over, at the speed you choose, and it travels in templates and template packs.
Try a free animated sticker or logo sting from LottieFiles in a lower third. Known limit: files that use expressions are refused (export them with expressions baked into keyframes).

New since 0.74.0-beta.1: transition styles, in the Effects add-on. Put the playhead on a dissolve, or double-click one, and the Transitions page shows a tile for each style: a dip to black, a flash, slides and pushes from any side, and 20 wipes, from straight wipes and a clock to a star and the unicorn horn. Click one to use it; wipes have Softness and Reverse. Press T to add a dissolve at the cut nearest the playhead.

Try a few wipes on clips you know, change the softness, undo, and render the project to check it plays as the preview did. Known limits: no zoom, spin or blend styles yet, and the tiles are drawings of each style, not your clips. With GPU acceleration on, a wipe can stutter at Full preview quality; Half plays it smoothly. A saved project with wipes keeps their shapes in a small ustudio-wipes folder beside it.

New since 0.73.1-beta.1: effects, in the Effects add-on. Open the inspector (the round button at the picture's top right) and press E: every effect is a tile showing your clip with it on. Point at one to try it on the picture, click to add it, then change it on the Effects page. Pin values at the playhead to make them change over time, save a set of effects as a look (five brand looks come with it), copy and paste effects between clips, and hold \ or press Compare to see before and after.

Try adding a few effects to a clip, keyframing one, applying a brand look to several clips at once, and dragging a look onto the picture. On a wide window the inspector now sits beside the picture instead of over it. Known limits: the Effects add-on isn't in this download yet (builds from source include it); effects can't be masked, and there are no wipes yet. The first run checks every effect in the background for a few minutes; tiles say "checking…" until then.

New since 0.73.0-beta.1: a crash is fixed. With GPU acceleration on, the editor could close when you paused, sought or played around a dissolve, especially while the computer was busy. GPU acceleration still starts off in this download; turn it on in Settings › Performance › Hardware to try it.
Try GPU acceleration on with dissolves, pausing and seeking around them, at Full and Half preview scale.

New since 0.72.0-beta.1: caption colours and top placement. Subtitle files that colour words white, lime, cyan, red, yellow, magenta, blue or black keep those colours, and captions the file puts at the top of the picture show there, in a top caption style. Both are written back out when you export captions.
Try a subtitle file from a video site that uses coloured speakers or top captions. Known limit: other colours, left/right positions and sizes from the file are still ignored.

New since 0.71.1-beta.1: update from template. A title made from a template now remembers it; when you open the title in U Stu Titles after its template has changed, a bar offers Update, which takes the new design and keeps your field text. Ctrl+Z takes it back.
Try making a title from one of your templates, editing the template, then reopening the title. Known limit: titles made before this version aren't offered updates.

New since 0.71.0-beta.1: GPU acceleration now starts off in this download, while a crash it can cause is being fixed. If you want it, turn it on in Settings › Performance › Hardware; your choice stays through updates.
Try playback and export with it off as usual. Known issue: with GPU acceleration on, the editor can still close unexpectedly when you pause or seek around a dissolve; turning it off avoids that.

New since 0.70.0-beta.1: caption export. Select a caption and click Export Captions… on the Title page; name the file .srt or .vtt. Every caption goes in, in time order, with your fixes to the words, bold, italic, underline and speakers.

Try importing a subtitle file, fixing a few lines, exporting it, and loading the new file in a video player or re-importing it. Known limit: a file's own positions and colours are still ignored on import.

New since 0.69.3-beta.1: captions. Import a subtitle file (.srt or .vtt) and every line becomes a caption on its own track at the top, all styled by one caption title you can restyle at once. Bold, italic, underline and WebVTT speakers are kept; unreadable lines are left out and reported.

Try importing a subtitle file from a video site or your captioning tool, restyle the caption title, and fix a line's words on the Title page. Known limits: captions can't be exported back to a subtitle file yet, and a file's own positions and colours are ignored.
New since 0.67.1-beta.1, the last published beta:

ul.li: A crash is fixed: with GPU acceleration on, pausing could close the editor when a clip and a copy of it played on different tracks at once (for example a rotated picture-in-picture over the original, in Half preview).
Template packs, in the Titles add-on: in U Stu Titles' template gallery, Save as Pack… shares your templates as one file, and Open Pack… installs someone else's.
New Title in a project you haven't saved yet keeps its title in your default project folder, your Videos folder or U Stu's data folder, never loose in your home folder.

description.p: Try pausing over a copied or rotated picture-in-picture with GPU acceleration on, and saving and opening a template pack. Install the Titles add-on of this same version with the app. Known limits: U Stu Share, the helper for sharing packs online, isn't in this download, so Browse Shared and Publish don't appear.
New Title in an unsaved project no longer creates a folder straight in your home folder: it uses your default project folder, your Videos folder, or U Stu's own data folder, in that order.
U Stu Share now wears the same Unicorn Tears colours as the editor and U Stu Titles.

New since 0.68.0-beta.1: U Stu Share, a separate helper for sharing template packs online (browse and install packs, publish your own). It's the only U Stu program that goes online, and only when you ask. The shared catalogue isn't online yet, so this beta can't reach it; U Stu Titles shows Browse Shared and Publish only where the helper is installed.
New since 0.67.1-beta.1:

ul.li: Template packs: in U Stu Titles' template gallery, Save as Pack… makes a .zip or .tar.gz of your templates to share, and Open Pack… shows what a pack holds, then installs it as a section of its own. Remove Pack… takes it out again.

description.p: Try saving a few of your templates as a pack, then opening it again (on another computer too). A pack that isn't safe (files outside it, links, fonts it may not share) is refused with the reason. Known limits: sharing packs online and updating a title from its template are still coming.
New since 0.65.1-beta.1:

ul.li: Title templates: New Title (Shift+T) puts a title at the playhead and opens U Stu Titles with a gallery of 29 built-in designs (lower thirds, badges, cards, end screens, countdowns, stream alerts). Save your own as templates, and rename, duplicate or delete them under My Templates.
A T button in the header (between Render and Settings) opens U Stu Titles: the selected title clip, or a new title from the gallery.
The Help button is a plain question mark.
The editor opens maximised, and the Render button is narrower so the project title has room.

description.p: Try New Title with a few templates, fill in their fields on the Title page, and save one of your own as a template. Titles need the Titles add-on installed next to the app. Known limits: template packs (sharing templates as a file) and updating a title from its template are still coming.

New in this beta: titles, as an add-on. Install the Titles add-on file next to the app (see Installing in the docs; it needs this exact app version), then restart U Stu. Settings › Drop-ins lists it, and a Title page appears for title clips.

Things to try: import a title (.ustitle file) onto a track above your video, fill in its fields on the Title page, open it with Edit Title (Ctrl+Shift+T) to change it in U Stu Titles, Bake it into a video file, and Export it on its own with transparency for OBS.
Known limits: the template gallery and New Title are still coming, so you start from an existing .ustitle file. U Stu Titles opens from the editor only; it has no app menu entry of its own yet.
New in this beta:

ul.li: GPU acceleration (Settings › Performance › Hardware): the preview and renders use the graphics chip, so several moved or scaled tracks play smoothly at full size. The app checks the GPU at start and falls back to the processor by itself if anything goes wrong.
Hardware video decoding, used together with GPU acceleration, takes more load off the processor.
Single-key shortcuts no longer fire while you type in a text field (Space in a settings field used to start playback).

description.p: Try a project with three or more moved, scaled or cropped tracks with GPU acceleration on and off. With it on, soft edges and dissolves look slightly brighter; that is how the GPU blends, and renders match the preview. Known limits: rotated clips still use the processor, and titles come as a separate add-on that isn't packaged yet.
New in this beta:

ul.li: A moved image sequence can be relinked: pick any of its images, or search a folder. It may be numbered from somewhere else now.
Image sequences get proxies, like video (unless they're transparent).
Video with transparency (ProRes 4444, WebM with alpha, QuickTime Animation) has clean edges over other tracks.
Colours are right in the preview and in renders: HD footage used to come out slightly off (reds duller, cyans with a red tint).
Open Log Folder now opens the folder the first time too, with this session's log selected.
Pick the project's background colour (click the title in the header bar): it shows wherever no clip covers the frame, in the preview and in renders.
Clips of another shape than the project (4:3, phone video) play much faster.
Exports at another size than the project place moved and fitted pictures correctly.
Transparent pictures (PNG stills, rotated or scaled clips) have clean edges over video: no more dark or coloured fringe.

description.p: New in this beta:

ul.li: Import Image Sequence… (Ctrl+Alt+I): numbered images such as frame_0001.png, frame_0002.png… become one clip, one image per frame. Pick any image of the sequence.

description.p: The app is now called U Stu Video Editor. Try the image sequences with one rendered from an animation or 3D tool. Known limits: a moved sequence can't be relinked yet (import it again), and sequences don't get proxies.
New since the previous beta:

ul.li: Media browser badges: each file shows what it is (image, audio), its resolution (in cyan when it is larger than the project) and its state (missing, proxy, proxy being made).
The media browser stays quick with hundreds of files: it only redraws what changed.
The clip tooltip on the timeline no longer flashes on and off.
No more crackle in the first half second after pressing play on a large project.
Fixed a crash after changing the project frame rate and then undoing it.
A new app icon, and Help › About shows the new logo, the Unicorn Tears Project and the source code. The editor is now MIT-licensed.

description.p: Known issues:

ul.li: Image sequences (numbered PNG or JPEG files) can't be imported as one clip yet.
Three or more moved, scaled or rotated tracks may stutter at 1080p even at Half preview scale.

description.p: The first beta. Highlights since the previous build:

ul.li: Proxies: smaller copies of large footage for smooth editing, made in the background and switched on and off beside the preview scale. Renders always use the originals.

Clip transform: move, scale, rotate, crop and flip any picture with handles right on the preview, with snapping, arrow-key nudges, a right-click menu and an Edit Transform window. Pictures of another size or aspect are fitted and centred.
Auto preview scale plays at Half once a clip is transformed, so an overlay stays smooth at 1080p.
Help: collapsible sections that remember what you had open, and these release notes.
If something goes wrong, Help › About › Copy Diagnostics puts the versions and the last log lines on the clipboard for your report, and Open Log Folder shows the full logs.
